prompt: dustveil: A broad-winged moth of the Rot, grown as much as hatched: its pale wings are a living felt of fungal threads, dusted with spores, and they hang from it like a veil. It flies in short, fluttering hops, over walls and water alike, and drops to the ground to feed. Its grubs are timid things that nibble at sparse growth. The adults are not timid about anything: they eat cloth, wool first and then any natural fibre, worn or stored, and settle for grass only when nothing better is within reach. A tamed one can be shorn of a fine moth-silk, the fungal felt of its wings, provided the silk is kept well away from every other dustveil, which will eat that too. It is NOT an Earth animal: wings made of a felt of fungal threads instead of scaled membrane; wings dusted with spores; wings hang from the body like a veil.
